baslik_html: x47.c drains AI keys straight to the invoice
alt_satir: Billable requests skip your app and land on the provider's bill.
gorsel_html:
What is it?

Qrator Labs documented x47.c, a Windows botnet sold by WraithTools. Its panel lists 18 DDoS methods, one of them draining a victim's AI API credit with stolen keys.

  • Malwarex47.c (Windows)
  • Sold byWraithTools · $200 to $950
  • DrainsOpenAI · xAI keys
  • Also stealscookies, wallets, tokens

How it works

  1. Stealer grabs AI-site tokens.
  2. Operator feeds a key and model.
  3. Bots send billable requests direct.
  4. Provider bills you, logs stay flat.

Where the cost lands (representative)

Same hour, two counters that should match.

# your app's own logged calls
app_calls_0900 = 1,240
# provider usage, same hour
provider_calls = 9,880

Check it today

# where do live keys sit?
$ grep -rn "OPENAI_API_KEY" .env* .github/
# then diff provider usage vs app log
Requests skip your gateway, so rate limits never see them.

How to defend

  • Put a hard spend cap on every key.
  • Alert on provider usage vs app logs.
  • Rotate keys out of .env and CI vars.
  • Scope each key to one model.
Your logs stay flat while the bill climbs.
